Semantic Alignment: Aliasing, f32, and Indirect Calls

All of the rules below mirror the interpreter and the JS backend (combinedKind/aliasCallee), with JS as the oracle; unknown shapes keep the historical forced signed lowering, and only statically knowable shapes change behavior.

1. Kind Selection for the Compatibility Aliases div/rem/gt/lt/shr

Decided by operand kind: float first, then signed, otherwise unsigned:

AliasfloatunsignedOther (including unknown)
divsa_fdivsa_udivsa_sdiv
remsa_srem (same as JS)sa_uremsa_srem
gt / ltsa_fcmp_gt / sa_fcmp_ltsa_ugt / sa_ultsa_sgt / sa_slt
shrsa_lshrsa_lshrsigned→sa_ashr, otherwise sa_lshr

The result width follows the chosen helper (udiv/urem/lshr→unsigned 64, fcmp→1), and chained aliases propagate the resolved domain correctly. Text immediates also participate in kind determination (i64→signed, u64→unsigned, a parseable float→float).

2. The f32 Domain

  • fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv and fcmp_*: both sides statically f32→the 32-bit helper; one side f32 and the other not confirmed f64→the 32-bit helper + truncation of the unconfirmed edge (the verifier guarantees domain consistency, so the truncation is an identity; the typical source is an indirect call's return value); otherwise the f64 path (the f32 edge is promoted).
  • The recorded width of an f32 result and its emission must stay strictly in sync, otherwise a downstream fcmp picks the wrong domain.
  • 32-bit explicit lshr narrowing: sa_lshr(sa_srcmask(v,W,0), sa_band(b,31)), shifting i32 0xFFFFFFFF as a u32 (the demo 347 class). ashr needs no handling because sign extension and arithmetic shift commute.
  • When the ftable's return domains are all consistent, an indirect call's result width is seeded precisely (such as a single-callback f32 table), allowing fneg32/both32 to be selected; inconsistent tables stay unknown.

3. Indirect-Call Dispatch (Including Fix History)

A unified signature makes the function-pointer table precise (indices agree with the fn_idx/vtable constant encoding). The old implementation first computed uint64_t idx = f - 1000000 and then tested idx >= 0; the unsigned comparison was always true, so with an empty table every indirect call went to the trap. The current implementation:

if (f < 1000000ULL) { sa_trap("bad indirect callee"); }
{ sa_u64 idx = f - 1000000ULL;
  if (idx >= (sa_u64)(sizeof(sa_ftable) / sizeof(sa_ftable[0])))
    { sa_trap("bad indirect callee"); }
  if (sa_ftable[idx] == 0) { sa_trap("null indirect callee"); }
  return sa_ftable[idx](a0, a1); }

An empty table degenerates to sa_ftable[1] = {0} (a zero-length array is a GNU extension and would make the bounds check always false). pthread_spawn runs its entry synchronously on the host side via the dispatcher, so programs that call it likewise always carry the dispatch table.
